newsitem.title: USA: Ascend in Global One carrier system pact.
newsitem.headline: Ascend in Global One carrier system pact.

text.p: Ascend Communications Inc said on Monday it had agreed to a pact with Global One through which the multinational carrier will use and resell Ascend's core line of remote access concentrator equipment.

Remote access concentrators are the central office equipment used by telecom carriers and Internet Service Providers (ISPs) to handle thousands of simultaneous incoming calls and outgoing from Internet customers.
Global One is the international joint venture of Sprint Corp, France Telecom and Deutsche Telekom AG.
Financial terms were not disclosed in a statement announcing the deal and a spokesman declined to comment, saying Ascend does not reveal the amounts of such contracts.

But Ascend said Global One has already installed more than 50 of Ascend's remote access concentrator systems for national phone carriers known as PTTs, as well as Internet Service Providers and businesses around the world.

A spokeswoman for Ascend declined to comment on when the company expected to begin recognizing revenue from these installations. She did say the 50 systems would be followed by additional deployments of Ascend equipment in the future.

Ascend also said that Global One in Brazil had recently selected Ascend's MAX & MAX TNT Wide Area Network (WAN) access switches for an internal backbone network as part of an Internet/Intranet service program it will offer customers.
Global One Brazil plans to use this network infrastructure to offer dial-up Internet access services to carriers and ISPs, the company said.
"Global One is rapidly emerging as one of the major forces in multinational Internet services," said Mory Ejabat, president and chief executive of Ascend Communications.

"All of the installations around the world have gone extremely well, and we are looking forward to working with Global One on a greatly expanded scale as they continue to grow their business," he said.
Global One offers integrated voice and data services to a customer base consisting largely of telecommunications carriers and largely multinational corporate companies.
It has more than 3,000 employees operating from 1,200 offices, or "points of presence" in more than 65 countries.
